theater: 薩爾瓦多－宏都拉斯邊境拉烏尼翁地

battle.name: 足球戰爭
battle.theater: 薩爾瓦多－宏都拉斯邊境拉烏尼翁地
battle.brief: 足球戰爭是薩爾瓦多與宏都拉斯於1969年7月因世界盃資格賽衝突而引發的國際戰爭，交火由球場蔓延至邊境及城鎮，延續數日。英國海軍Torpedo boat（魚雷艇）自1877年列裝後，負責近岸巡邏、警戒與快速追擊，反映當時海軍對海上快速反應能力的重視。

kit.name: 魚雷艇
kit.history: 英國海軍把Torpedo boat納入近海與沿岸作戰體系，以高速、淺吃水和魚雷武器執行巡邏、追擊、警戒及封鎖任務，是海防力量中重要的高速海上反應單位。

countries: 1969年7月14日至30日，交戰的兩國是宏都拉斯與薩爾瓦多，戰事完全發生在兩國共有的約三百四十公里邊境線上。宏都拉斯由民選總統拉蒙·比耶達·莫拉萊斯主持國政，但國家機器的實際主導權握在陸軍總參謀長古斯塔沃·阿道佛·皮諾·蘇亞索與參謀本部手中，軍方自五月底即以邊防營、步兵營為主體徵召預備役，把兵力集中在馬拉加省與薩爾瓦多接壤的東部山區與邊境公路。薩爾瓦多方面，掌權者是軍人出身的總統菲德爾·卡斯特羅·赫南德斯，國防部直接指揮駐邊營與首都地區的營連，防守依托山脊、咖啡園、村鎮與河流渡口。兩個國家的常備軍規模都不大，都沒有可獨立運作的裝甲師，也沒有能持續取得制空權的航空兵，因此整場衝突的本質是沿山脊與公路進行的步兵、迫擊砲與榴彈砲的消耗戰。宏都拉斯在兵源、車輛與美援彈藥的補充上佔有明顯優勢，薩爾瓦多則在陣地工事、熟悉地形與持久抵抗上較為硬朗。
countriesEn: The two belligerents in July 1969 were Honduras and El Salvador, and every round of the war was fought along the roughly 340-kilometre border the two countries share. In Honduras the elected president Ramón Villeda Morales headed the government, but effective control of the state rested with the chief of the army, General Gustavo Adolfo Pino Suazo, and the general staff. From the end of May the military called up reserves and concentrated the main body of its frontier and infantry battalions in the eastern highlands of Morazán and along the roads facing El Salvador. In El Salvador power belonged to the soldier-president Fidel Castro Hernández; the ministry of defence directly commanded the border battalions and the companies of the capital area, and the defence rested on ridges, coffee plantations, villages and river crossings. Neither army was large, neither fielded an independent armoured division, and neither could sustain air superiority, so the conflict was fundamentally a war of attrition between infantry, mortars and howitzers along ridges and roads. Honduras held a clear advantage in manpower, vehicles and the resupply of American ammunition, while El Salvador was harder and more persistent in field fortification, local knowledge of the ground and delaying actions.
people: 真正決定戰局的是四個人。宏都拉斯總統拉蒙·比耶達·莫拉萊斯最初不贊成跨境用兵，因為他擔心與尼加拉瓜、古斯達黎加的邊境爭端同時升高；他與總參謀長古斯塔沃·阿道佛·皮諾·蘇亞索之間的裂痕，正是皮諾在六月底至七月間繞過內閣、直接以無線電與各營營長聯絡並在7月23日下達攻擊命令的原因，比耶達·莫拉萊斯在同年10月被迫去職。薩爾瓦多總統菲德爾·卡斯特羅·赫南德斯面對邊境連日衝突，起先仍企圖用外交手段把球賽爭議與戰事脫鈎，最後在軍方要求下同意全面反擊，並授權國防部統一調度邊防部隊。國際足總祕書長史坦利·勞斯在檢視兩場爭議比賽的判決後公開批評執法為可恥，並要求足總紀律處理，這番表態反而讓雙方政府都把球賽的判決視為不能再退讓的國家榮譽問題。此外，兩國足協的主席與教練班底多由軍方或親軍方人士把持，比賽因此不再是體育事務，而是軍隊士氣與徵兵渠道的延伸；兩國代表隊的球員、教練與裁判在7月14日之後，也被捲入難以區分對手與敵人的狀況。
peopleEn: Four men shaped the outcome. Ramón Villeda Morales, the Honduran president, at first opposed any cross-border use of force because he feared simultaneous trouble on the borders with Nicaragua and Costa Rica; the fracture between him and General Gustavo Adolfo Pino Suazo, chief of the army, explains why Pino Suazo, between late June and July, bypassed the cabinet, spoke by radio directly to battalion commanders and issued the order for the attack of 23 July, and why Villeda Morales was pushed out of office in October of the same year. Fidel Castro Hernández, the Salvadoran president, faced several days of incidents on the frontier and at first tried to use diplomacy to separate the football dispute from the fighting, before agreeing to a general counter-offensive and entrusting the ministry of defence with unified control of the border troops. Stanley Rous, secretary general of FIFA, reviewed the decisions in the two disputed matches, called the refereeing shameful in public and demanded disciplinary action; that statement in turn persuaded both governments that the refereeing could no longer be treated as a sporting matter open to compromise. The presidents of the two football associations and most of the coaching staffs were officers or officials closely tied to the armed forces, which turned the fixtures into an instrument of army morale and of recruitment, and after 14 July the players, coaches and officials of the two national teams were caught in a situation in which opponent and enemy could no longer be told apart.
kits: 兩軍的裝備以美軍戰後標準配發為主。步兵的骨幹槍械是M1加蘭德步槍，口徑.30-06，彈藥為M1903與M1908式步槍彈；機關槍為勃朗寧M1918A2自動步槍、M2勃朗寧.50重機槍與M1919A4輕機槍，近戰有M1928A1與M1A1湯普森衝鋒槍，配.45 ACP手槍彈。連屬火力是60毫米M2與M3迫擊砲及81毫米M1迫擊砲，前者用M49砲彈，後者用M61系列81毫米砲彈；營以上的火力是105毫米M2A1榴彈砲與155毫米M114榴彈砲，以M1型榴彈為主。車輛包括M35型2.5噸六輪卡車、M54型載重卡車與M151 MUTT四分之一噸吉普，野戰通訊使用SCR-300與SCR-625無線電及野戰電話。兩國陸軍編制表內都列有M3史都華輕型坦克與M8灰獵犬裝甲車，但車齡老、車況差、油料不足，真正投入邊境作戰的數量極少，多數戰史都認為裝甲未能左右戰局。空軍任務以偵察、聯絡與後勤運輸為主，機型為道格拉斯C-47與塞斯納180、185這類輕型機，全程沒有制空權之爭。
kitsEn: The equipment of both armies was based on standard American post-war issue. The infantry backbone was the M1 Garand rifle in .30-06, fed by M1903 and M1908 ammunition; machine guns included the Browning M1918A2 automatic rifle, the M2 Browning .50-calibre heavy machine gun and the M1919A4 light machine gun, while close-quarter weapons were the M1928A1 and M1A1 Thompson submachine guns firing .45 ACP. Company-level firepower was the 60 mm M2 and M3 mortars and the 81 mm M1 mortar, the former firing M49 rounds and the latter M61-series 81 mm rounds; artillery above battalion level was the 105 mm M2A1 and the 155 mm M114 howitzer, firing mainly M1 high-explosive shells. Vehicles were M35 2.5-ton six-wheel trucks, M54 cargo trucks and M151 MUTT quarter-ton jeeps, with SCR-300 and SCR-625 radios and field telephones for command. Both order-of-battle lists included M3 Stuart light tanks and M8 Greyhound armoured cars, but their age, poor condition and fuel shortages meant very few actually took part in the frontier fighting, and most campaign accounts agree that armour never decided the war. Air tasks were reconnaissance, liaison and logistics with Douglas C-47 transports and light types such as the Cessna 180 and 185; there was no contest for air superiority.
tactics: 7月23日的進攻採取典型的邊境突進樣式：宏都拉斯先以連為突擊群，選擇阿馬波拉一帶的林間小徑、阿馬蒂略渡口附近的淺灘與通往內陸的數條車行山道同時突入，步兵在迫擊砲與105毫米榴彈砲的集中火力掩護下推進；砲兵採射擊後立即轉移的做法，避免被薩爾瓦多以短程迫擊砲從反斜面觀察射擊，同時以工兵在渡河點架設便橋或以橡皮艇渡過Lempa河下游與邊界溪流。薩爾瓦多則以營為單位據守山脊與咖啡園，構築交通壕、機槍巢與環形掩體，利用村鎮縱深與道路窄隘限制對方車輛，並以小分隊在夜間實施反擊與側擊，使宏都拉斯的推進隊形不斷被切斷。通信在山區主要依靠無線電與報話員，命令常需以人跑腿送達，前後方配合因此延遲數小時。補給是整場戰役最脆弱的一環：糧食、油料與砲彈依靠單一公路上的車隊輸送，砲彈存量有限，前線附近必須設置小型彈藥庫，傷員則以卡車沿公路逐段後送。雙方都沒有大規模空襲或縱深打擊，戰線始終貼著邊境推移。
tacticsEn: The offensive of 23 July followed the classic pattern of a frontier coup de main. Honduras formed assault groups at company level and entered at several points at once: wooded tracks around Amapola, the shallows near the El Amatillo crossing, and several vehicle tracks leading into the interior. Infantry advanced under concentrated fire from mortars and 105 mm howitzers; artillery used shoot-and-scoot tactics, displacing immediately after each salvo to avoid Salvadoran short-range mortar fire observed from reverse slopes, while engineers bridged the crossings or ferried troops across the frontier watercourses, including the lower Lempa channel and the smaller streams, with rubber boats. El Salvador defended in battalion strength on ridges and among coffee plantations, with communication trenches, machine-gun pits and ring positions, using the depth of the villages and the narrowness of the roads to slow vehicles, and launching night counter-attacks and flank attacks with small detachments so that the Honduran advance was repeatedly cut. Communications in the hills depended on radio and runners, and orders often took hours to reach the front. Logistics were the weakest part of the campaign: food, fuel and shells moved by single-file truck convoys on one road, mortar and howitzer ammunition stocks were limited and small ammunition dumps were laid out close to the front, and wounded were evacuated stage by stage by truck. Neither side mounted large air attacks or deep strikes; the line of contact moved along the border itself.
data: 時間線非常清楚：1969年5月26日，小組第一場在塔古西加爾帕的蒂布里西奧·卡里亞斯國家體育場舉行，宏都拉斯以3比0取勝；6月30日第二場移師聖薩爾瓦多，薩爾瓦多以2比0扳平；第三場定於7月14日在同一座國家體育場重賽，爭議判決引發看台衝突，比賽在開賽約三十分鐘後中止，各家記述略有出入，多數認為記分牌停在宏都拉斯3比2領先。足球戰爭自7月14日算起，至7月28日達成停火，7月29至30日雙方撤軍完畢，實際大規模交火集中在7月23日至28日，前後約六天。兵力方面，宏都拉斯投入的野戰部隊一般被估計為一萬五千至三萬人，薩爾瓦多可投入的兵力約八千至一萬人，另有邊防警與後方勤務單位。傷亡沒有可靠的官方總計，常被引用的估計從數百人到上千人不等，宏都拉斯方面的陣亡通常被認為低於薩爾瓦多。紅十字會國際委員會的登記顯示，戰後第一週有數千名薩爾瓦多人越境進入瓜地馬拉，整場衝突期間進入宏都拉斯的薩爾瓦多人數在六萬至十萬之間。
dataEn: The chronology is precise. On 26 May 1969 the first match of the group was played at the Tiburcio Carías national stadium in Tegucigalpa and Honduras won 3–0; the second leg was moved to San Salvador on 30 June and El Salvador won 2–0; the third was scheduled to be replayed at the same stadium on 14 July, and the disputed decisions set off fighting in the stands, the match being stopped after roughly half an hour of play, accounts differing slightly, most of them giving Honduras 3–2 at the moment of suspension. The football war is counted from 14 July to the ceasefire of 28 July, with both sides completing their withdrawal on 29 and 30 July, the heavy fighting concentrated in the six days from 23 to 28 July. On the ground, the Honduran field force committed is generally estimated at 15,000 to 30,000 men, against 8,000 to 10,000 available to El Salvador, with border police and rear-service units holding guard and support duties. No reliable official count of casualties exists; the figures most often quoted range from several hundred to more than a thousand, and Honduran dead are usually considered fewer than Salvadoran. International Committee of the Red Cross registrations show several thousand Salvadorans crossing into Guatemala in the first week after the war, and between sixty thousand and a hundred thousand entering Honduras over the course of the conflict.
cause: 直接導火線是國際足總1970年世界盃外圍賽的東區小組。宏都拉斯與薩爾瓦多被分在同一組，三場比賽的兩回合都出現爭議：6月30日聖薩爾瓦多的比賽裡，薩爾瓦多在終場前獲得一記罰球並由罰球踢進第二球，宏都拉斯球員與隨隊者事後包圍裁判；同一組第一場則有人指薩爾瓦多應得的罰球被漏判，雙方各自認定執法偏袒。7月14日的重賽成為所有怨氣的出口，看台互毆後比賽被叫停，兩國足協互相指責，國際足總祕書長史坦利·勞斯公開斥責判決。更深層的原因有四條：一是邊界爭議多年，焦點包括帕哈里托、梅西利亞與阿馬蒂略渡口一帶的土地與Lempa河下游水道，雙方都主張對方越界開墾與越線巡邏；二是薩爾瓦多農工長期到宏都拉斯邊境棉田季節性移工，一旦邊境關閉，後果立即落在邊境村鎮與軍隊身上；三是1960年代後期兩國軍人政府都倚重足球俱樂部與聯邦作為合法性與徵兵渠道，比賽成了軍隊士氣與民族主義的裝置；四是冷戰格局下的美援分配、軍方擴張，以及共產黨在薩爾瓦多的影響，使邊境摩擦有機會被升級為國家之間的開戰。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the CONCACAF qualifying group for the 1970 FIFA World Cup. Honduras and El Salvador were drawn into the same group, and both legs produced controversy: in the match at San Salvador on 30 June, El Salvador was awarded a penalty late in the game and scored the second goal from it, and Honduran players and their entourage surrounded the referee afterwards; in the first leg in the other direction there were claims that a penalty due to El Salvador was not given, each side concluding that the referee had favoured the other. The replay on 14 July became the outlet for all the accumulated grievance: after the stands fought, the match was stopped, the two associations accused one another, and the FIFA secretary general Stanley Rous publicly branded the decisions shameful. Four deeper causes lie behind it. First, the border dispute had run for years, focused on El Pajarito, La Mesilla and the land and the lower Lempa channel around the El Amatillo crossing, each side accusing the other of cultivating and patrolling beyond the line. Second, Salvadoran farm labour moved seasonally into the cotton fields of the Honduran border, and once the frontier was closed the consequences fell at once on border villages and army posts. Third, the military governments of the late 1960s in both countries leaned on football clubs and federations as instruments of legitimacy and of recruitment, so fixtures became devices for army morale and nationalism. Fourth, the Cold War distribution of American aid, military expansion and the influence of the communists in El Salvador gave border friction the chance to be turned into a war between states.
impact: 戰役的破壞集中在邊境百里之內的村莊、道路、灌溉渠道與橋樑，宏都拉斯東部的阿馬波拉與薩爾瓦多的聖米格爾、烏蘇盧坦一線反覆遭砲擊，並有輕型機進行過少量投彈，雙方的田作、倉儲與道路被反覆破壞，邊境聚落整村遷徙，直到停火後數月才有人返回。評估損失的主要依據是紅十字會的救護記錄與聯合國查證團的報告，但沒有一方公布過可核對的陣亡名冊，宏都拉斯在停火協議中取得的，只是有限的戰俘交換與傷員遣返安排。政治效應長遠而尖銳：宏都拉斯從此把7月14日視為國家尊嚴日，至今仍是國定假日，軍方每年以閱兵與紀念演練重述那場勝利；薩爾瓦多軍方的聲望則因戰後仍靠戒嚴與警察鎮壓維持秩序而更形孤立，數年後的革命把這段戰爭記憶成軍政不義的證詞。體育上，宏都拉斯在1970年世界盃小組賽於墨西哥城客場以1比0擊敗墨西哥，被許多人視為這場戰爭的延伸與補償，而Football War這個名字則從此固定在兩國的記憶與外交場合裡。
impactEn: The damage was concentrated in the villages, roads, irrigation channels and bridges within a hundred kilometres of the frontier; Amapola in eastern Honduras and the San Miguel and Usulután lines in El Salvador were repeatedly shelled, and a small number of sorties by light aircraft added to the damage, farm buildings, depots and roads on both sides being repeatedly destroyed, whole border settlements being evacuated and only returning months after the ceasefire. The Red Cross relief records and the report of the United Nations fact-finding mission are the main basis for measuring the human cost, but neither side ever published a verifiable casualty roll, and what Honduras obtained under the ceasefire agreement was limited prisoner exchange and the phased return of the wounded. The political effects were long and sharp. Honduras has treated 14 July as the Day of National Dignity, still a public holiday, and the army marks the anniversary with parades and commemorative exercises that retell the victory; in El Salvador the military's prestige was further undermined by the fact that order was still kept by decree and police repression after the war, and the revolution that came years later turned the memory of the football war into evidence of military wrongdoing. In sport, Honduras beating Mexico away in Mexico City in the group stage of the 1970 World Cup was read by many as an extension and compensation for the football war, and the name Football War has since been fixed in the memory and the diplomatic language of the two countries.
result: 停火在7月28日達成，協議的核心是各自撤回7月23日以前的防線位置，宏都拉斯部隊於7月29至30日逐步撤出薩爾瓦多東部，邊境回到戰前狀態，沒有任何領土變更，兩國也沒有簽下永久性的邊界修改條約，爭議留下的問題轉入外交程序處理。國際足總否決了7月14日那場中斷比賽的賽果，未再安排重賽，宏都拉斯因此取得小組第一，於1970年與墨西哥、加拿大、千里達及托貝哥同組作戰，最終從小組出線いきました參加墨西哥城世界盃，薩爾瓦多則未能晉級。戰後數月內，兩國簽署邊界與睦鄰條約並成立混合勘界小組，界線標識與土地爭議的處理因此延續多年。對軍人而言，這是一場代價慘重而戰果有限的戰爭：宏都拉斯靠較大兵力與較好補給換取了邊境的短期安寧，薩爾瓦多則以陣亡與撤退換取了首都與主要城市的完好；對兩個國家而言，7月這十七天把球場上的記分變成了無法折算的帳目。
resultEn: The ceasefire was reached on 28 July; its core was the withdrawal of both sides to the positions held before 23 July, Honduran forces pulling out of eastern El Salvador step by step on 29 and 30 July, the frontier returning to its pre-war state, no change of territory, and no permanent border modification signed, the outstanding questions passing to diplomatic channels. FIFA voided the result of the interrupted match of 14 July and ordered no replay, so Honduras took the group and in 1970 played in the final round alongside Mexico, Canada and Trinidad and Tobago, emerging from the group to reach the World Cup in Mexico City, while El Salvador did not qualify. Within months of the ceasefire the two governments signed a border and friendship agreement and created a mixed demarcation commission, and the marking of the frontier and the settlement of outstanding claims ran on for years afterwards. For the soldiers this was a costly war with limited results: Honduras exchanged a larger force and better logistics for a short-term peace on the frontier, El Salvador paid in dead and retreat to keep its capital and principal cities intact; for both countries, those seventeen days of July turned a score on a football field into a ledger that could not be balanced.
